**Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.**

My brother brought a few rice while coming from the market.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'a few rice while'.**

__
 
• **Rice** is an **uncountable noun.**

• **Example**:

• Correct sentence__: *My brother brought **a little / some** rice while coming from the market.*
 
• Hence, the correct answer is** option 3**.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.**

Optimist
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Idealist**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Let us look into the meaning of the given words:

 
• **Optimist: **a person who tends to be hopeful and confident about the future. (आशावादी व्यक्ति)

 
 
• **Example**- As an optimist, I always believe tomorrow will be better than today.
 
 
 
• **Idealist:** is one who believes more in an ideal world rather than the real one. (आदर्शवादी व्‍यक्ति)
 
 
• **Example**- The idealist was certain that he would win the race, even though he came in last place in his previous competitions.
 
 
 
• **Distinct:** not identical; separate. (स्‍पष्‍ट; सुव्‍यक्त)
 
 
• **Example- **There was the distinct smell of something burning.
 
 
 
• **Critic:** a person who expresses an unfavorable opinion of something. (दोष बताने वाला व्‍यक्ति; आलोचक, समीक्षक)
 
 
• **Example**- He was a stern critic but an extremely kindly man.
 
 
 
• **Pessimist:** a person who believes that the worst will happen. (निराशावादी व्‍यक्ति)
 
 
• **Example**- He is a pessimist and a defeatist.
 
 

 

Thus, the synonym of **'Optimist' is 'Idealist'.**

questions.question:

Obvious
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Evident'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

Let us look into the meaning of the given words:

• **Obvious:** easily perceived or understood. (जो आसानी से दिखाई दे या समझ में आए; स्‍पष्‍ट)

 
 
• **Example**-* Her doctor immediately noticed the obvious signs of the disease.*
 
 
 
• **Evident:** clearly seen or understood; obvious. (स्‍पष्‍ट (दीखने में या सोच में); सुस्‍पष्‍ट, प्रकट)
 
 
• **Example- ***He signed his name with evident satisfaction.*

• **Vague:** of uncertain, indefinite, or unclear. (अस्पष्ट)
 
 
• **Example-* ****She felt a vague sense of uneasiness when she was around him. *
 
 
 
• **Various:** different from one another. (विभिन्‍न, विविध)
 
 
• **Example**- *She was mimicking the various people in our office. *
 
 

Thus, the synonym of the given word **'Obvious' is 'Evident:'.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.**

Mr Kansal has been living in Delhi __since__ 10 years.
questions.solution:
Option 3 is the right answer: For.

The given sentence gives a time span of '10 years'. So, the correct time expression is 'for'.

Let us look into the other options one by one:

 
• For is used to show the duration of an action.—for 2 years.
 
• Until is used to show when an action ends.—until 2 p/m/ / until he was satisfied.
 
• From & To--is always used together. They show when the action begins and when it ends. “—from 1 a.m. to 3 a.m.

Correct sentence: Mr Kansal has been living in Delhi for 10 years.
